A recent social media post claims that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been selected as the new chairman of the World Health Organization (WHO). This assertion has gained traction on various platforms, leading to confusion and curiosity about the leadership structure of WHO and its relationship with international political figures. This article examines the validity of the claim, provides background on the WHO’s leadership, and clarifies Narendra Modi’s actual roles and responsibilities.

The World Health Organization, a specialized agency of the United Nations, is tasked with directing and coordinating international health efforts. Its leadership comprises a Director-General, currently Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, who was re-elected in 2022 for a second five-year term. The WHO’s governance also includes the World Health Assembly, which consists of delegates from its 194 member states and is presided over by a president and vice-presidents, typically chosen from among health ministers or senior health officials of member nations. The position of “chairman” is not a formal title within the WHO’s top leadership; rather, the Assembly may elect a president to oversee sessions, but this role is distinct from executive leadership.

Narendra Modi is the incumbent Prime Minister of India, one of the world’s largest democracies. Since assuming office in 2014, Modi has played a significant role in shaping India’s domestic and foreign policies, including its approach to public health challenges such as the COVID-19 pandemic. However, his official responsibilities are confined to leading the Indian government; he does not hold a formal position within United Nations agencies such as the WHO.

Fact-checking the core claim reveals several inaccuracies. Firstly, there is no official announcement or record from either the Indian government or the WHO indicating that Narendra Modi has been selected as chairman or for any equivalent role within the organization. The WHO’s selection process for leadership roles is transparent and involves nominations and elections by member states, typically culminating in the appointment of health experts or senior officials, not sitting heads of government. Moreover, the role of chairman or president at the World Health Assembly is a rotating position held by member state delegates for the duration of the Assembly, and again, is not equivalent to overall executive leadership.

The spread of this misinformation may stem from confusion over India’s active participation in global health forums or Modi’s prominent international profile. India has played a constructive role in WHO meetings and initiatives, and Indian health officials have sometimes held leadership positions within the organization. However, these appointments are distinct from the claim that the Prime Minister himself has assumed a top role within WHO.

In summary, the social media claim that Narendra Modi has been selected as the new chairman of the World Health Organization is unfounded and incorrect. The WHO’s leadership is determined by member state processes and governed by specific rules that do not accommodate the appointment of sitting national heads of government to executive roles. Narendra Modi continues to serve as India’s Prime Minister with no official position within the WHO.

article_content:
In a recent social media post, a claim was made that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that 10 million COVID-19 patients have been treated for free in India. This assertion warrants closer examination to assess its accuracy, provide context, and analyze the broader implications for India’s healthcare response during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Background and Context

India, with its vast population of over 1.4 billion, faced one of the world’s most daunting challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic. The government implemented a range of measures to combat the virus, including lockdowns, vaccination drives, and healthcare support programs. One of the most notable initiatives was the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), a national health insurance scheme launched in 2018, which aims to provide free healthcare services to economically vulnerable families. When COVID-19 struck, the government expanded the scheme to include COVID-19 testing, treatment, and hospitalization costs.

Fact-Checking the Claim

The core claim under scrutiny is that Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated 10 million COVID-19 patients have received free treatment in India. The Indian government, through PM-JAY and other state-sponsored programs, did indeed offer free treatment for COVID-19, especially for those in economically weaker sections. Reports from government briefings and official statements highlight that millions have benefited from free healthcare services during the pandemic, including COVID-19 testing and hospitalization.

Numerically, the figure of 10 million (1 crore) patients aligns with periodic updates given by government sources. Throughout 2021 and 2022, Prime Minister Modi and other officials cited milestones in the number of beneficiaries who received free treatment for COVID-19 under PM-JAY and other schemes. It should be noted, however, that these figures often include cumulative data from all beneficiaries of free healthcare, not exclusively those treated for COVID-19. Nevertheless, official communication has indicated that millions of COVID-19 patients specifically received free treatment under these programs.

Analysis and Nuances

While the claim reflects a broad truth about India’s commitment to providing free treatment to COVID-19 patients, it is important to recognize nuances. The total number may represent cumulative figures from various health schemes, some of which predate the pandemic and cover a range of illnesses beyond COVID-19. Additionally, the definition of “free treatment” can vary, as not all hospitals or states implemented the scheme uniformly. Reports from some regions highlighted delays, limited coverage, or out-of-pocket expenses for certain patients.

Despite these challenges, India’s large-scale response and mobilization of resources did result in millions of COVID-19 patients receiving free treatment, particularly in government hospitals and through PM-JAY. The claim that Prime Minister Modi said 10 million patients benefited is consistent with official statements and government data released during and after the pandemic’s peak.

Conclusion

The statement attributed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi about 10 million COVID-19 patients being treated free of cost in India is broadly accurate and reflects the scale of the government’s healthcare response. However, the figure should be understood as an approximation, subject to periodic updates and variations in implementation across states. Overall, India’s efforts to provide free treatment to millions of COVID-19 patients under various government programs stand as a significant public health achievement, even as challenges in consistent execution remain.

Én av de mest fremste initiativene var Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), et nasjonalt helseforsikringssystem lansert i 2018, som har til mål å gi gratis helsevård til økonomisk svake familier. Da covid-19 rammet landet, utvidet regjeringen skjemaet til å inkludere covid-19-testing, behandling og sykehusopphold.

Fakta-undersøkelse av påstanden

Den sentrale påstanden som undersøkes er at statsminister Narendra Modi sa at 10 millioner covid-19-pasienter har fått behandling for gratis i India. Den indiske regjeringen, gjennom PM-JAY og andre statlige programmer, tilbydde virkelig gratis behandling for covid-19, spesielt for de økonomisk svake. Rapporter fra regjeringens briefinger og offisielle uttalelser viser at millioner har fått nytte av gratis helsevård under pandemien, inkludert testing og sykehusopphold.

Numerisk er tallet på 10 millioner (1 crore) pasienter i tråd med de periodiske oppdateringene fra regjeringens kilder. Under 2021 og 2022 har statsminister Modi og andre offentlige figurene nevnt milepæler i antallet fordelede som har fått gratis behandling for covid-19 under PM-JAY og andre programmer. Det bør merkes at disse tallene ofte inkluderer kumulative data fra alle fordelede av gratis helsevård, ikke bare de som ble behandlet for covid-19. Likevel har offentlige kommunikasjoner indikert at millioner av covid-19-pasienter spesifikt har fått gratis behandling under disse programmene.

Analyse og nuanser

Selv om påstanden reflekterer en bred sannhet om Indias kommittment til å gi gratis behandling til covid-19-pasienter, er det viktig å erkjenne nuanser. Det totale tallet kan representere kumulative tall fra ulike helseprogrammer, noen av hvilke forekommer før pandemien og dekker en rekke sykdommer utenfor covid-19. I tillegg kan definisjonen av «gratis behandling» variere, da ikke alle sykehus eller stater implementerte programmet uniformt. Rapporter fra noen regioner pekte på forsinkelser, begrenset dekning eller utstedte penger for visse pasienter.

Selv med disse utfordringene hadde Indias store skala-tilgang og mobilisering av ressurser ført til at millioner av covid-19-pasienter hadde fått gratis behandling, spesielt i offentlige sykehus og gjennom PM-JAY. Påstanden om at statsminister Modi sa at 10 millioner pasienter hadde fått nytte av dette er i tråd med offisielle uttalelser og regjeringens data som ble fremlagt under og etter pandemien.

Konklusjon

Påstanden som tilskrives statsminister Narendra Modi om at 10 millioner covid-19-pasienter ble behandlet uten kostnad i India er i bred forstand nøyaktig og reflekterer skalaen på regjeringens helsevårdsrespons. Likevel bør tallet forstås som en tilnærming, som er underkastet periodiske oppdateringer og variasjoner i implementering over stater. I sin helhet står Indias anstrengelser til å gi gratis behandling til millioner av covid-19-pasienter under ulike regjeringelige programmer som et betydelig offentlig helseopnåelse, selv om utfordringer i konsekvent gjennomføringen fortsatt eksisterer.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, governments worldwide undertook massive relief efforts to support their populations through unprecedented economic challenges. In India, central authorities announced a range of welfare measures, including direct financial assistance to vulnerable citizens. A recent social media post claims that Indian Home Minister Amit Shah stated the government transferred financial aid of Rs 530 million into the bank accounts of 410 million people during the pandemic, which, according to the post, equates to just Rs 1.29 for each recipient. This article examines the accuracy and context of this claim.

**Background and Context**

India, with its vast population, faced significant logistical and economic hurdles during the pandemic. In March 2020, the government announced the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Yojana (PMGKY), a relief package aimed at providing food grains, direct cash transfers, and other support to the poor and vulnerable. The cash component was intended to reach millions of beneficiaries, including farmers, women, senior citizens, and daily wage workers.

**The Claim**

The post asserts that Home Minister Amit Shah claimed Rs 530 million was distributed to 410 million people, resulting in an average payout of Rs 1.29 per person. This figure is presented as evidence of an inadequate government response.

**Fact-Checking the Figures**

First, it is crucial to verify if Amit Shah made such a statement and whether the figures cited are accurate.

Publicly available statements from government officials, including Amit Shah, have referenced large-scale direct benefit transfers during the pandemic. However, the amounts reported by the government have been significantly higher than Rs 530 million. Government press releases and speeches often cite figures in the range of Rs 30,000 crore (Rs 300 billion) or more, distributed to hundreds of millions of beneficiaries.

If we consider the arithmetic in the post: dividing Rs 530 million by 410 million people results in Rs 1.29 per person. This calculation is mathematically correct based on the numbers provided. However, the figures themselves do not align with official records.

**Analysis of Government Transfers**

According to official data, the government claimed to have transferred cash benefits ranging from Rs 500 to Rs 2,000 per person to various groups under different schemes. The total amount disbursed reportedly exceeded Rs 300,000 million (Rs 3 lakh crore), far above the Rs 530 million claimed in the post.

It is possible that the figure of Rs 530 million cited in the social media post is a misinterpretation, mistranslation, or typographical error. For instance, the original statement may have referred to "Rs 530 billion" (Rs 53,000 crore), which would result in a per-person benefit of approximately Rs 129, a figure much closer to reported averages for certain beneficiary groups.

**Conclusion**

The claim that the Indian government distributed only Rs 530 million among 410 million people, resulting in a per-person payment of Rs 1.29, is not supported by official data or public statements from the Home Minister. The government reported far larger transfers, and even a basic review of the relief measures shows that individual payments to beneficiaries were typically much higher. The figures in the post likely result from a misreading or misreporting of the actual amounts involved. Therefore, the core claim of the post is inaccurate and misrepresents the scale of India’s COVID-19 financial aid.

A recent social media post is circulating with the claim that a video depicts the last COVID-19 patient exiting from a hospital in New Zealand. The post has gained traction, with many viewers sharing it as a sign that New Zealand has officially ended its fight against the coronavirus. This article examines the accuracy of the claim, the context surrounding it, and the current COVID-19 situation in New Zealand.

The video in question typically features hospital staff lining a corridor, some applauding as a patient—often portrayed as the “last COVID-19 patient”—is wheeled or walks out of the building. The emotional scene is framed as a moment of national triumph, and many viewers have interpreted it as evidence that New Zealand has eradicated COVID-19 from its hospitals.

To analyze this claim, it’s important to review New Zealand’s history in managing COVID-19. The country was widely praised for its swift and strict measures in the early stages of the pandemic. In 2020, New Zealand implemented one of the world’s toughest lockdowns and closed its borders, managing to eliminate community transmission for prolonged periods. This led to international headlines and several viral moments, including instances where hospitals celebrated the discharge of their last COVID-19 patient at certain points in the pandemic.

However, these moments did not necessarily indicate the end of COVID-19 in New Zealand. Instead, they marked temporary milestones—such as the last active case in a particular hospital or region being discharged, rather than the absolute end of all COVID-19 hospitalizations nationwide. Due to new variants and global travel, New Zealand, like many countries, experienced subsequent waves of COVID-19 infections and hospitalizations after these celebrated moments.

Upon close review, the video being circulated does not provide verifiable evidence that it captures the last COVID-19 patient in all of New Zealand leaving a hospital. In some cases, such videos have been posted by individual hospitals marking their own milestones, and not a national event. Furthermore, official health data from New Zealand shows that COVID-19 cases, while significantly reduced from peak levels, have not been completely eradicated, and hospitalizations have occurred intermittently as new variants have emerged.

Additionally, New Zealand’s Ministry of Health has not announced a definitive end to COVID-19 hospitalizations or declared that the last patient has exited the country’s hospitals. Health authorities continue to monitor cases and encourage vaccination and public health measures as needed.

In summary, while the video captures a positive moment for a hospital and its staff, the claim that it shows the very last COVID-19 patient leaving a hospital in all of New Zealand is misleading. Such celebrations have occurred at various points in the pandemic, often on a local or regional basis, rather than representing a national conclusion. As of the latest updates, COVID-19 remains present in New Zealand, and hospitalizations, while rare, have not been eliminated entirely.

A video circulating on social media claims to show quarantined patients dancing inside a COVID-19 center in Mumbai. The footage, widely shared on various platforms, depicts a group of people wearing masks and casual clothing, moving energetically to upbeat music in a large hall with rows of beds in the background. The post suggests that the individuals participating in the dance are patients under quarantine during the COVID-19 pandemic and that the facility is located in Mumbai.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to examine the context in which such videos emerged, the circumstances of COVID-19 quarantine centers in Mumbai, and any corroborating reports from credible sources.

During the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, Mumbai, one of India’s hardest-hit cities, established numerous quarantine and isolation centers to house patients who tested positive for the virus, particularly those with mild or asymptomatic cases. These centers were set up in large venues such as sports complexes, schools, and exhibition halls, often comprising rows of beds and medical staff on site. The mental health of patients in isolation became a significant concern for authorities and healthcare workers, prompting various initiatives to keep morale high and alleviate anxiety.

In response to these challenges, several centers in Mumbai and across India introduced recreational activities, including music, dance, and group games, to help quarantined individuals cope with the stress of isolation. Videos and news stories from the period document instances where healthcare workers and patients engaged in collective dance sessions, sometimes led by staff members, as a form of exercise and emotional support. These activities were generally well-received and shared on social media as uplifting examples of resilience during crisis.

Upon close review, the video in question matches the description and visual characteristics of Mumbai’s large COVID-19 quarantine centers seen during 2020 and 2021. The beds, layout, and the presence of multiple masked individuals align with known images from such facilities. Furthermore, the practice of organizing dance sessions in these centers is consistent with reports from the time.

However, it is important to note that videos of this nature were not unique to Mumbai. Similar scenes occurred in quarantine facilities elsewhere in India and even internationally. While the claim that the video shows quarantined patients dancing in a COVID-19 center is plausible and supported by documented practices, the specific identification of the location as Mumbai depends on visual clues within the video and confirmation from local authorities or media reports.

In conclusion, the core claim that quarantined patients participated in dance sessions within Mumbai’s COVID-19 centers is credible and matches known practices during the pandemic. The video likely depicts such an event, although without further verification, it is possible that similar footage from other locations could be misattributed. Nonetheless, the use of dance as a tool for morale and community within quarantine centers is a well-documented aspect of Mumbai’s pandemic response.

ਮੈਡੀਆ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਕੋਰੋਨਾ ਵਾਇਰਸ ਮਹਾਮਾਰੀ ਦੇ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚ ਪੱਧਰ 'ਤੇ, ਮੁੰਬਈ, ਭਾਰਤ ਦੇ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਪ੍ਰਭਾਵਿਤ ਸ਼ਹਿਰਾਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਇੱਕ, ਕੋਰੋਨਾ ਵਾਇਰਸ ਪਾਜ਼ੀਟਿਵ ਰੋਗੀਆਂ, ਖਾਸ ਕਰਕੇ ਹੱਲੋ ਅਤੇ ਅਸੰਘਟਿਤ ਮਰੀਜ਼ਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਘਰ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਰੱਖਣ ਲਈ ਕੁਆਰੰਟੀਨ ਅਤੇ ਅਲੱਗਾਂਕਣ ਸੈਂਟਰ ਸਥਾਪਿਤ ਕੀਤੇ ਗਏ ਸਨ। ਇਹ ਸੈਂਟਰ ਬੱਠੀਆਂ ਵਾਲੀਆਂ ਬੁਲੰਦੀਆਂ, ਸਕੂਲਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਹਾਲਾਂ ਜਿਹੇ ਵੱਡੇ ਸਥਾਨਾਂ 'ਤੇ ਸਥਾਪਿਤ ਕੀਤੇ ਗਏ ਸਨ, ਜਿਹਨਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੁਲੰਦੀਆਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਲਾਈਨਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਮੈਡੀਕਲ ਸਟਾਫ ਦੀ ਉਪੇਕਸ਼ਾ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਸੀ। ਇਸਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਹੀ, ਰੋਗੀਆਂ ਦੀ ਮਨੋਵਿਗਿਆਨਕ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਅਧਿਕਾਰੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਿਹਤ ਕਰਮੀਆਂ ਦੀ ਚੰਗੀ ਚਿੰਤਾ ਬਣੀ ਰਹੀ, ਜਿਸ ਕਾਰਨ ਵਿਭਿੰਨ ਪ੍ਰਯੋਗ ਕੀਤੇ ਗਏ ਸਨ ਤਾਂ ਕਿ ਮਨੋਰੰਜਨ ਦੇ ਮੌਕੇ ਦੇ ਕੇ ਮਾਨਸਿਕ ਚਿੰਤਾ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਬੰਧ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾ ਸਕੇ।

ਇਸ ਚੁਣੌਤੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਜਵਾਬ ਵਿੱਚ, ਮੁੰਬਈ ਅਤੇ ਭਾਰਤ ਦੇ ਵੱਖ-ਵੱਖ ਸੈਂਟਰਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਨੋਰੰਜਨ ਦੇ ਕਾਰਜਾਂ, ਜਿਵੇਂ ਕਿ ਗਾਣਾ, ਨਾਚ, ਅਤੇ ਕੂੜ੍ਹੇ ਖੇਡਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ। ਇਸ ਸਮੇਂ ਦੇ ਵੀਡੀਓ ਅਤੇ ਖਬਰਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਕਈ ਅਧਿਐਨ ਦਰਜ ਕੀਤੇ ਗਏ ਹਨ, ਜਿੱਥੇ ਸਿਹਤ ਕਰਮੀ ਅਤੇ ਰੋਗੀ ਮਿਲ ਕੇ ਨਾਚ ਦੇ ਸੈਸ਼ਨ ਲੈ ਰਹੇ ਸਨ, ਜਿਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਕਈ ਵਾਰੀ ਕਰਮੀ ਨੇ ਨੇਤ੃ਤਵ ਕੀਤਾ। ਇਹ ਕਾਰਜ ਆਮ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ ਮਾਨਯੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਸੋਸ਼ਲ ਮੀਡੀਆ 'ਤੇ ਸ਼ੇਅਰ ਕੀਤੇ ਗਏ ਸਨ, ਜੋ ਮਹਾਮਾਰੀ ਦੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਦੀ ਮਾਨਸਿਕ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਦੇ ਸਥਾਪਤ ਉਦਾਹਰਣ ਦੇ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੰਨੇ ਗਏ ਸਨ।

ਸੰਪਾਦਨ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ, ਕੁਆਰੰਟੀਨ ਹੋਏ ਰੋਗੀਆਂ ਨੇ ਮੁੰਬਈ ਦੇ ਕੋਰੋਨਾ ਵਾਇਰਸ ਸੈਂਟਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਾਚ ਸੈਸ਼ਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਭਾਗ ਲੈਣ ਦਾ ਦਾਅਵਾ ਸੰਭਵ ਅਤੇ ਮਹਾਮਾਰੀ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਦਸਤਾਵੇਜ਼ ਕੀਤੇ ਗਏ ਪ੍ਰਯੋਗਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਮੇਲ ਖਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਵੀਡੀਓ ਨੂੰ ਇਸ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਇਕ ਘਟਨਾ ਦਾ ਦਰਸਾਉਣਾ ਸੰਭਵ ਹੈ, ਹਾਲਾਂਕਿ ਇਸ ਦੀ ਪੁਸ਼ਟੀ ਬਗੈਰ ਇਸ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਵੀਡੀਓ ਦੇ ਹੋਰ ਸਥਾਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਅਸਥਾਪਤ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਦਾ ਦਾਅਵਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਹਾਲਾਂਕਿ, ਕੁਆਰੰਟੀਨ ਸੈਂਟਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਨੋਰੰਜਨ ਅਤੇ ਸਮੁਦਾਇਕ ਵਿਚ ਨਾਚ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਮੁੰਬਈ ਦੀ ਮਹਾਮਾਰੀ ਦੇ ਜਵਾਬ ਵਿੱਚ ਇੱਕ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ ਪਹਿਲੂ ਹੈ।

A video circulating on social media claims to show a COVID-19 patient collapsing on the streets of Pune and being taken away in an ambulance. The footage, which has garnered significant attention and concern among viewers, depicts an individual suddenly falling to the ground while bystanders gather around. Shortly after, an ambulance arrives, and medical personnel are seen attending to the person before transporting them away.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to examine both the content of the video and the context in which it has been shared. The post’s core assertion is twofold: first, that the video is from Pune, and second, that the individual is a COVID-19 patient who collapsed due to the virus.

COVID-19, caused by the novel coronavirus, is primarily a respiratory illness. While some patients do experience severe symptoms, including shortness of breath and, in rare cases, sudden collapse due to respiratory failure or cardiac complications, the vast majority of COVID-19 cases do not result in people collapsing suddenly in public spaces. Throughout the pandemic, videos and stories of patients allegedly collapsing in public have periodically surfaced, often accompanied by alarming claims.

Upon closer inspection of the video, several details warrant scrutiny. The environment, including signage, vehicles, and the attire of bystanders, can sometimes provide clues about the location. However, many videos shared online are not accompanied by verifiable timestamps or location data. In this case, there is no clear evidence visible in the video itself—such as identifiable landmarks or street signs—conclusively indicating it was filmed in Pune.

Furthermore, local authorities in Pune have not issued any statements confirming such an incident occurred. In previous instances where similar videos have gone viral with claims of COVID-19 patients collapsing, subsequent investigations have sometimes revealed that the footage was either from a different time, another location, or unrelated to COVID-19 altogether. Some videos have depicted individuals fainting due to heatstroke, exhaustion, or unrelated medical emergencies.

The response by ambulance and medical personnel in the video does align with standard protocols for responding to a medical emergency during the pandemic, as healthcare workers are required to take precautions when dealing with any patient in public. However, this does not in itself confirm the cause of the incident.

Given these factors, the social media post’s claim that the video shows a COVID-19 patient collapsing in Pune cannot be independently verified. Without official confirmation, supporting evidence, or additional context, it remains unclear whether the person in the video was indeed suffering from COVID-19, or whether the incident took place in Pune as claimed.

In conclusion, while the video does show an individual collapsing and being attended to by medical personnel, the assertion that this is a COVID-19 patient in Pune is unsubstantiated. Viewers should exercise caution before accepting such claims at face value and await confirmation from credible sources. Misleading or unverified information can contribute to unnecessary panic and stigma during public health crises.

article_content:
A video circulating on social media purports to show a doctor from Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital claiming that if a person can hold their breath for a “longer period” without discomfort, they do not have Coronavirus (COVID-19). The video has gained widespread attention, with many users sharing it as a quick self-test for COVID-19. In this article, we examine the origins of this claim, its medical validity, and whether breath-holding serves as a reliable indicator for COVID-19 infection.

**Background of the Viral Claim**

The “breath-holding test” first gained popularity in the early months of the COVID-19 pandemic. At that time, misinformation spread rapidly due to public anxiety and a lack of widespread testing. The test’s premise is simple: if an individual can take a deep breath and hold it for at least 10 seconds (sometimes up to 20 or 30 seconds) without coughing, discomfort, or difficulty, they supposedly do not have COVID-19 or lung fibrosis. According to the social media post, a doctor from the reputable Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai allegedly endorses this method.

**Analysis of the Claim**

The core assertion is that “If you can hold your breath for a longer period without discomfort, you don’t have Coronavirus.” This statement is not supported by scientific evidence or guidelines issued by international or national health authorities.

COVID-19 is caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which can lead to a wide range of symptoms, including cough, fever, fatigue, sore throat, and in severe cases, shortness of breath and pneumonia. However, many people who are infected with the virus remain asymptomatic or experience only mild symptoms. Some might not develop breathing difficulties until the illness has progressed. Therefore, the absence of breathing discomfort during a breath-holding test does not rule out COVID-19 infection.

Additionally, the ability to hold one’s breath can be influenced by various factors unrelated to respiratory infections. These include age, baseline lung function, physical fitness, anxiety levels, and pre-existing medical conditions such as asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). A healthy individual without COVID-19 but with poor lung function may still struggle with breath-holding, while a person in the early stages of COVID-19 or with a mild case may hold their breath without any noticeable issues.

No credible medical institution, including Breach Candy Hospital, has endorsed the breath-holding test as a diagnostic tool for COVID-19. Major health organizations recommend laboratory-based testing (such as PCR or rapid antigen tests) to diagnose COVID-19. Relying on unproven self-assessment techniques can be dangerous, leading people to ignore symptoms, delay seeking medical attention, or inadvertently spread the virus.

**Conclusion**

The video’s claim that holding your breath for a long period without discomfort means you do not have Coronavirus is false and misleading. There is no scientific basis for using breath-holding as a diagnostic tool for COVID-19. Individuals concerned about COVID-19 should follow reputable health guidelines, seek proper diagnostic testing, and consult qualified healthcare professionals rather than relying on viral social media advice.

**ବିରଳ ଦାବିର ପ୍ରାରମ୍ଭିକ ବିଷୟ**

"ଶ୍ୱାସରୋଧନ ପରୀକ୍ଷା" କୋଭିଡ୍-୧୯ ମହାମାରୀର ପ୍ରାରମ୍ଭିକ ମାସରେ ଲୋକମାନଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଲୋକପ୍ରିୟ ହୋଇଥିଲା। ସେତେବେଳେ ଜନତାର ଆଶଙ୍କା ଏବଂ ପ୍ରସାରିତ ପରୀକ୍ଷା ଅଭାବ କାରଣରୁ ଅନୁଚିତ ତଥ୍ୟର ପ୍ରସାରିତ ହୋଇଥିଲା। ଏହି ପରୀକ୍ଷାର ମୂଳ ଧାରଣା ଏହି ଯେ ଯଦି କେହି ଏକ ଗଭୀର ଶ୍ୱାସ ନେଇ କମ୍ବା ୧୦ ସେକେଣ୍ଡ (କେତେକ ପରିସ୍ଥିତିରେ ୨୦ କି ୩୦ ସେକେଣ୍ଡ) ଧରି ରଖି କଷ୍ଟ ବିନା ହେଲେ, କଷ୍ଟର ଅଭାବ ବା କଷ୍ଟ ବିନା କୋହଳରେ ରହିପାରିବେ, ତେବେ ସେ କୋଭିଡ୍-୧୯ ବା ଫୁସ୍ଫୁସର ପ୍ରାକୃତିକ ପ୍ରାକୃତିକ ଅବସ୍ଥା ବିନା ରୋଗୀ ନୁହେଁ। ଏହି ସୋସିଆଲ ମୀଡିଆ ପୋଷ୍ଟରେ ମୁମ୍ବାଇର ପ୍ରଶାସନିକ ବ୍ରେଚ୍ କାନ୍ଡି ହସ୍ପିଟାଲର ଏକ ଡାକ୍ତର ଏହି ପଦ୍ଧତିକୁ ପ୍ରଶଂସା କରିଛନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ଦାବି କରାଯାଇଛି।

ଅନ୍ୟ କାରଣଗୁଡିକ ମଧ୍ୟ ଶ୍ୱାସରୋଧନ କରିବା କ୍ଷମତାକୁ ପ୍ରଭାବିତ କରିପାରେ, ଯଥା: ବୟସ, ମୂଳ ଫୁସ୍ଫୁସର କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ, ଶାରୀରିକ ଶକ୍ତି, ଆଶଙ୍କା ପରିମାଣ ଏବଂ ପ୍ରାକୃତିକ ଚିକିତ୍ସା ଅବସ୍ଥା, ଯଥା: ଏସ୍ଟ୍ରମା ବା ଅପସ୍ଥାନିକ ଫୁସ୍ଫୁସର ଅବସ୍ଥା (COPD)। କୋଭିଡ୍-୧୯ ରୋଗର ପ୍ରାରମ୍ଭିକ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟ ବା ମଧ୍ୟମ ରୋଗର ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି କେବେ କେବେ ଶ୍ୱାସରୋଧନ କରିବା ବିନା କୋହଳରେ ରହିପାରିବେ, କିନ୍ତୁ କୋଭିଡ୍-୧୯ ରୋଗର ଅଭାବ ହୋଇଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ଯଦି ମଧ୍ୟ ମୂଳ ଫୁସ୍ଫୁସର ଅବସ୍ଥା ହୋଇଥାଏ, ତେବେ ସେ ଶ୍ୱାସରୋଧନ କରିବା ବେଳେ କୋହଳ ଅନୁଭବ କରିପାରିବେ।

article_content:
A widely shared social media post claims that the Ministry of AYUSH has removed Dr. Mujahid Hussain from service because he banned Baba Ramdev's medicine, Coronil. The post suggests a direct link between Dr. Hussain’s alleged ban on Coronil and his removal, implying retaliation by the Ministry of AYUSH in favor of Baba Ramdev’s product. This article examines the accuracy of these assertions and provides context on the controversy surrounding Coronil.

**Background on Coronil**

In early 2021, Baba Ramdev’s Patanjali Ayurved launched Coronil, a herbal medicine purported to boost immunity and claimed by its promoters as a “cure” for COVID-19. The launch was met with significant controversy. Medical authorities, including the Indian Medical Association, criticized Patanjali for making unsubstantiated claims about Coronil’s efficacy against COVID-19. The Ministry of AYUSH, which oversees traditional and alternative medicine in India, intervened and clarified that Coronil could only be marketed as a “supporting measure” for COVID-19 management and not as a cure.

**Who is Dr. Mujahid Hussain?**

Dr. Mujahid Hussain is not a widely recognized senior official within the Ministry of AYUSH. There is no record in public domain sources, government press releases, or news coverage of a Dr. Mujahid Hussain holding a prominent role in the Ministry, nor is there any official communication regarding his employment status or termination.

**Examining the Claim**

The social media post asserts two main points: first, that Dr. Mujahid Hussain banned Coronil, and second, that he was removed from service by the Ministry of AYUSH as a result.

A thorough search of public records, Ministry of AYUSH notifications, and credible news reports reveals no evidence that Dr. Mujahid Hussain was ever involved in policy decisions regarding Coronil. The Ministry’s official position on Coronil was communicated through formal statements, not individual bans by specific officers. The regulatory process for herbal and alternative medicines typically involves review by panels and committees, not unilateral bans by single officials.

Regarding the alleged removal from service, there is no confirmed information or official announcement about Dr. Mujahid Hussain being terminated from the Ministry of AYUSH. Such administrative actions, especially those involving high-profile controversies, are usually publicized through government notifications or media coverage, none of which support the claim.

**Analysis and Conclusion**

The claim that Dr. Mujahid Hussain was removed from service by the Ministry of AYUSH because he banned Coronil is unsubstantiated. There is no evidence of Dr. Hussain holding an official post relevant to the Coronil controversy, no record of any individual ban imposed on Coronil by him, and no official statement about his removal from service.

The controversy over Coronil did involve scrutiny and intervention by the Ministry of AYUSH, but actions were taken through official channels and collective regulatory mechanisms, not by individual officials acting alone. The narrative presented in the social media post appears to be misleading and not supported by verifiable facts.

In summary, the core claim of the post lacks factual basis and should be regarded with skepticism. Readers are advised to seek information from authoritative sources and avoid spreading unverified claims on social media.

Široko šírený sociálny súborový príspevok tvrdí, že Ministerstvo AYUSH odstránilo lekára Dr. Mujahid Hussaina z služby, pretože zakázal liek Baba Ramdeva, Coronil. Príspevok naznačuje priamo spojenie medzi príspevkom Dr. Hussaina o zakázaní Coronila a jeho odstránením, čo implikuje odškodnenie Ministerstva AYUSH v prospech výrobku Baba Ramdeva. Tento článok skúma presnosť týchto tvrdení a poskytuje kontext okolo kontroverzie okolo Coronila.

**Pozadie o Coronil**

Na začiatku roku 2021 spoločnosť Patanjali Ayurved Baba Ramdeva predstavila Coronil, herbálny liek, ktorý sa tvrdilo zvyšuje imunitu a ktorý sa podľa propagátorov vyslovil ako „lepivo“ pre ochorenie COVID-19. Spustenie bolo veľmi kontroverzné. Zdravotnícke orgány, vrátane Indian Medical Association, kritizovali Patanjali za nedokázané tvrdenia o účinnosti Coronila proti ochoreniu COVID-19. Ministerstvo AYUSH, ktoré zodpovedá za tradičné a alternatívne liečivá v Indii, zasiahlo a upresnilo, že Coronil sa môže predávať iba ako „podpora“ na manažment ochorenia COVID-19 a nie ako lečivo.

**Kto je Dr. Mujahid Hussain?**

Dr. Mujahid Hussain nie je známy ako významný štátny úradník v Ministerstve AYUSH. Nie je žiadna veľká zverejnena zdrojová informácia, vládne tlačové vyhlášky alebo novinové správy, ktoré by ukazovali, že Dr. Mujahid Hussain držal významnú funkciu v Ministerstve, ani nie je žiadna oficiálna komunikácia o jeho pracovnom stave alebo odchod.

**Skúmanie tvrdenia**

Sociálny súborový príspevok tvrdí dva hlavné body: prvým je, že Dr. Mujahid Hussain zakázal Coronil, a druhým, že bol odstránený z služby Ministerstvom AYUSH ako výsledok tohto.

Podrobný prehľad verejných záznamov, oznámení Ministerstva AYUSH a dôveryhodných novinových správ ukazuje, že žiadna dôkazná podpora nie je prítomná, že Dr. Mujahid Hussain bol niekedy zapojený do rozhodnutí o politike ohľadom Coronila. Oficiálna pozícia Ministerstva ohľadom Coronila bola komunikovaná prostredníctvom oficiálnych vyhlášok, nie jednotlivými zakázaniami konkrétnych pracovníkov. Regulačný proces pre herbálne a alternatívne liečivá zvyčajne zahŕňa hodnotenie výborov a komisí, nie jednotlivé zakázania jednotlivými úradníkmi.

Ohľadom príspevku o odstránení z služby nie je žiadna potvrdená informácia alebo oficiálna správa o tom, že Dr. Mujahid Hussain bol odvolaný z Ministerstva AYUSH. Takéto administratívne aktivity, najmä v prípadoch významných kontroverzií, sú zvyčajne zverejňované prostredníctvom vládnych oznámení alebo mediálnych správ, ktoré žiadne nepodporujú tento príspevok.

**Analýza a záver**

Tvrdenie, že Dr. Mujahid Hussain bol odstránený z služby Ministerstvom AYUSH, pretože zakázal Coronil, nemá dôkazy. Nie je žiadna dôkazná podpora, že Dr. Hussain držal oficiálnu funkciu, ktorá je spojená s kontroverzou okolo Coronila, žiadna záznam o individuálnom zakázaní Coronila, ktoré by mu prispôsobilo, a žiadna oficiálna správa o jeho odchode z služby.

Kontroverzia okolo Coronila zahŕňala skúmanie a zásah Ministerstva AYUSH, ale akcie boli vykonané prostredníctvom oficiálnych kanálov a kolektívnych regulačných mechanizmov, nie jednotlivými úradníkmi, ktorí pôsobili samostatne. Príbča, ktorú predstavil sociálny súborový príspevok, sa zdá byť výmyselná a nepodporovaná dôkazmi.

V závere, jadro príspevku nemá faktický základ a by malo byť považované za pochybné. Ľudia sú vyzvaní, aby informácie získali z autoritárnych zdrojov a zabránili šíreniu neoverených príspevkov na sociálnych sietiach.
